## Summary

SR bit 11, the Apollo bit, keeps E registers intact across task switches on a ROM-patched AmigaOS and enables the LineA instructions. User mode may set and clear it.

## Details

- Multitask & additional line-a instructions.
- ApolloOS always saves the new registers on task switching.
- A program that sets SR bit 11 keeps e-registers intact when switching task on an rom patched OS like amiga or coffin. The 080 allows it to be set in user-mode.
- Other bits will of course give a privilege exception as expected.
- LineA-instructions become valid when the apollo-bit in SR is set.
- LineA $a000..$a00f will not be used to be atari-os compatible.
- “LineA” instructions are: clr.q , mov3q , moviw.l , mov(s/z)
- Ori #$800,sr sets the apollo-bit.
- Andi #$f7ff,sr clears the apollo-bit.
- The apollo-bit affects only the program that sets it. Setting it and expecting another program to behave if the apollo-bit is set does not work.
- So restoring the bit on exit is not needed.

## Differences from AmigaOS / AROS / 68060

- On the 68000–68060, writing SR in user mode causes a privilege exception. On the 68080, `ori #$800,sr` and `andi #$f7ff,sr` are allowed in user mode.

## Do / Don't

- DO set the Apollo bit in your own program when you need it; it only affects the program that sets it.
- DON'T expect the Apollo bit set by one program to affect another.
